html:
Alexander Bustamante was the labour leader who became the first prime minister of independent Jamaica in 1962. He rose to fame in the labour unrest of 1938, which swept the island as it did much of the British Caribbean.

He founded the Bustamante Industrial Trade Union and in 1943 the Jamaica Labour Party, which won the first election held under universal suffrage in 1944. His cousin and rival Norman Manley led the People's National Party.

Bustamante campaigned for Jamaica to leave the West Indies Federation, and won the referendum of 1961. He led the island to independence in 1962. The two parties he and Manley founded have alternated in power ever since.
